card.title: 104th INFANTRY REGIMENT
card.flavorText: The 104th Infantry Regiment was a unit of the US Army.Its lineage traces back to 14 November 1639 and it stayed active until 2005. In January 1942 the 104th was put on coastal defense duty and their task was to secure landing bases in the North Atlantic and to prevent saboteurs landing on American beaches. In January 1943 the regiment received amphibious assault training, and finally on August 27th, 1944 the regiment, as part of the 26th Infantry Division, sailed to Cherbourg in France. The division entered combat in France in September 1944 when it landed at Cherbourg. The division was then assigned to the US Third Army under Lieutenant General George S. Patton, and after a few minor skirmishes it went on a full offensive in November. The division captured the towns Dieuze and Sarre-Union, and engaged in intense house-to-house combat before reaching the Maginot fortifications. It was then reassigned to III Corps and sent to Luxembourg in order to participate in the Battle of the Bulge. Later the division advanced into Austria and aided in the capture of Linz before overrunning the Gusen concentration camp before its destruction by German forces. The division halted its advance following the cease-fire order on May 4th, 1945.
